name: Linux & Shell
description: Working at the Linux command line: files and permissions, text processing, processes, networking tools and shell scripting.

nodes.name: Linux & distros
nodes.desc: Kernel vs distribution, the terminal and the shell.
nodes.summary: You will understand how the Linux kernel, distributions, terminals and shells fit together and why Linux is used so widely.

nodes.name: Shell basics
nodes.desc: Commands, arguments, ls, cd, pwd, tab completion and history.
nodes.summary: You will be able to run commands with options and arguments, move around the filesystem and work faster with completion and history.
topics: Navigating with ls, cd and pwd

nodes.name: Filesystem layout
nodes.desc: The directory tree, /etc, /home, /var, /usr and absolute vs relative paths.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find your way around the Linux directory tree and use absolute and relative paths correctly.

nodes.name: Getting help
nodes.desc: man pages, --help and reading command documentation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to look up how any command works using man pages, built-in help and other documentation sources.
topics: Finding commands with which and type

nodes.name: Working with files
nodes.desc: cp, mv, rm, mkdir, touch, globbing and viewing files.
nodes.summary: You will be able to create, copy, move, delete and view files and directories, using globbing to work on many at once.
topics: Copying and moving with cp and mv
Viewing files with cat, less, head and tail

nodes.name: Permissions
nodes.desc: rwx bits, chmod, chown, umask and sudo.
nodes.summary: You will be able to read and change Linux file permissions and ownership and run commands with elevated privileges using sudo.
topics: chmod with symbolic and octal modes

nodes.name: Users & groups
nodes.desc: Accounts, groups and /etc/passwd.
nodes.summary: You will be able to manage user accounts and groups and understand how Linux stores account information.

nodes.name: Links & inodes
nodes.desc: Inodes, hard links, symbolic links and disk usage.
nodes.summary: You will understand inodes and be able to create hard and symbolic links and check disk usage.
topics: Inspecting files with stat and ls -i
Disk usage with df and du

nodes.name: Pipes & redirection
nodes.desc: stdin, stdout, stderr, redirection and composing commands with pipes.
nodes.summary: You will be able to redirect standard input, output and error and chain commands together with pipes.

nodes.name: grep & find
nodes.desc: Searching file contents and the filesystem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to search file contents with grep and locate files by name, type, size or age with find.
topics: Finding files by name and type
find tests on size and modification time
Running commands on results with -exec and xargs

nodes.name: Regular expressions
nodes.desc: Basic and extended regex for grep and sed.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write basic and extended regular expressions to match text patterns in grep and sed.
topics: Quantifiers like star, plus and question mark

nodes.name: sed & awk
nodes.desc: Stream editing and column-oriented text processing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to transform text streams with sed and process column-based data with awk.
topics: Deleting and printing lines with sed

nodes.name: Processes & signals
nodes.desc: ps, top, kill, signals, job control and nohup.
nodes.summary: You will be able to inspect and control running processes, send signals and manage foreground and background jobs.
topics: Listing processes with ps and top
Job control with bg, fg and jobs

nodes.name: Package management
nodes.desc: Installing software with apt, dnf or pacman.
nodes.summary: You will be able to install, update and remove software with your distribution's package manager.
topics: Using apt on Debian and Ubuntu

nodes.name: Networking tools
nodes.desc: ping, curl, ss, dig and inspecting network connections.
nodes.summary: You will be able to diagnose network connectivity and inspect connections using common Linux networking commands.

nodes.name: SSH & remote work
nodes.desc: SSH keys, scp, rsync and working on remote machines.
nodes.summary: You will be able to log in to remote machines securely with SSH keys and transfer files with scp and rsync.

nodes.name: Bash scripting
nodes.desc: Variables, conditionals, loops, functions and exit codes in bash scripts.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write bash scripts with variables, conditionals, loops and functions that report success or failure through exit codes.

nodes.name: cron & services
nodes.desc: Scheduling jobs with cron and managing services with systemd.
nodes.summary: You will be able to schedule recurring jobs with cron and manage long-running services with systemd.

nodes.name: Environment & dotfiles
nodes.desc: Environment variables, PATH, shell configuration and dotfiles.
nodes.summary: You will be able to configure your shell environment with environment variables, PATH and dotfiles you can carry between machines.

nodes.name: Log analyzer project
nodes.desc: Write a script that parses server logs and reports top errors and visitors.
nodes.summary: You will write a shell script that parses server logs and reports the most common errors and the top visitors.

nodes.name: Backup script project
nodes.desc: Automate scheduled, rotating backups to a remote machine.
nodes.summary: You will automate scheduled, rotating backups of important files to a remote machine using shell tools.
topics: Remote copies with rsync over SSH
Scheduling with cron and logging results
